# Hanksville cluster — gap-closing pass (trip days 8–9, 10 Sep – 4 Oct 2028)

**Scope:** closes the Hanksville gaps left open by `research-trails.md` §4 and `research-logistics.md` §5.2–5.3.
**Written:** 2026-09-05. **Do not edit other research files — this supersedes the GAP markers in those two sections only where stated below.**

## Headline: the two "no retrievable source" items are now sourced from BLM itself

The BLM **Henry Mountain Field Station** publishes short self-guided-tour PDFs for exactly these
destinations. Prior lanes never found them because they are not linked from
`blm.gov/visit/factory-butte-recreation-area` — they hang off the field-station office page under
"Popular Destinations". Index page: <https://www.blm.gov/office/henry-mountains-field-station>

| Destination | Official BLM PDF |
|---|---|
| Blue Valley Spire + Cow Dung Road + Bentonite Hills + Burpee Quarry | <https://www.blm.gov/sites/default/files/docs/2026-04/Blue%20Valley_Burpee%20Quary.pdf> |
| Moonscape Overlook | <https://www.blm.gov/sites/default/files/docs/2026-04/Moonscape%20Overlook%202025.pdf> |
| Little Egypt | <https://www.blm.gov/sites/default/files/docs/2026-04/Little%20Egypt.pdf> |
| Factory Butte SRMA brochure (OHV areas, acreages, contacts) | <https://www.blm.gov/sites/default/files/documents/files/BLMUtahFinalFactoryButte_Brochure.pdf> |

Both PDFs were downloaded and text-extracted directly (not read through a summariser), so the
quotes below are verbatim.

**Mile-marker frame of reference used throughout:** UT-24 mile posts *decrease* heading west out of
Hanksville. Hanksville sits at roughly **MP 116.3**. This reconciles every source: MP 113 ≈ 3.4 mi
west (Cow Dung Rd), MP 109–110 ≈ 6.3–7.3 mi west (Blue Valley Spire), MP 106 ≈ 10.3 mi west
(Factory Butte Rd), and BLM's "Factory Butte is 12 miles west of Hanksville" for the butte itself.

## 1. Blue Valley Spire ("Long Dong Silver Spire") — CLOSED

Two independent sources agree on the access and disagree only on the walking distance.

### Access — verbatim from BLM

> "**Blue Valley Spire** — BLM Rd #1574 is located between mile markers 109 and 110 on the north side
> of Hwy 24. In approximately half a mile in a road branches left for an additional 0.7 miles to a
> wooden fence serving as the trailhead. Round trip the hike is 1.6 mi and sun exposed, bring water
> is even on this short hike."

Source: <https://www.blm.gov/sites/default/files/docs/2026-04/Blue%20Valley_Burpee%20Quary.pdf>

### Trailhead coordinates and road detail — Road Trip Ryan

- **Trailhead coordinates: 38°22'10"N, 110°49'55"W** (UTM 12S 514680E 4246818N).
- "Head west on UT-24 from Hanksville for about **7 miles to mile post 109.35**. There is a dirt road
  leaving UT-24 here on the right (north) side of the highway." Follow it **1.2 miles** north to the
  **road-closure sign, which is the trailhead**.
- Road surface/vehicle, verbatim: "The road is accessible by **medium clearance vehicles, except when
  wet. Do NOT try to visit when wet, as you will definitely tear up the road and likely get stuck!**"
- **Round trip 2.3 miles**; elevation range **4,400–4,573 ft = 173 ft of gain**. Rated "**easy hike**".
- Route type, verbatim: "**Follow the now closed road north into the valley**" — i.e. you walk an old
  closed two-track, then **social trails** lead the last bit to the tower. It is **not a built trail
  and not signed as one**; it is also **not cross-country navigation** — you are on an obvious roadbed.
- Water: "None, bring all you need."

Source: <https://www.roadtripryan.com/go/t/utah/san-rafael-swell/long-dong-silver>

### Answers to the six questions asked

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| Trailhead coordinates | **38°22'10"N, 110°49'55"W**; turn off UT-24 at **MP 109.35**, north side, onto **BLM Rd 1574** |
| Road surface to trailhead | **1.2 mi of dirt/clay two-track** (0.5 mi, then bear left 0.7 mi), ending at a **wooden fence / road-closure sign** |
| Does a 2WD passenger car reach it? | **Dry: yes for a crossover/SUV; marginal for a low sedan.** RTR's wording is "medium clearance", not "any vehicle". A RAV4/Equinox-class rental clears it easily when dry. **Wet: no vehicle, full stop.** |
| Round trip distance | **1.6 mi (BLM)** vs **2.3 mi (RTR, with GPS track)**. Plan on **2.3 mi / 3.7 km** — the larger number is the one backed by a mapped track. |
| Gain | **~173 ft / 53 m.** Effectively flat. |
| What the "trail" is | A **closed roadbed** walked to its end, then **social trails** to the spire base. No cairns needed, no exposure, no scrambling. |

**Verdict for an 11-year-old:** this is the easy one. Flat valley floor, 173 ft of gain, no drop-offs.
The only hazards are heat and full sun exposure with zero shade. Do it early morning or the last hour.

**Legality/land status: confirmed BLM.** The route is on a BLM-numbered road (#1574) and BLM publishes
it as a public self-guided destination — this closes `research-trails.md` §4.5's open question (c).

**Composition note (unsourced observation, flagged as such):** the spire is a fragile bentonite/shale
pinnacle. `GAP:` BLM does not state a height for the spire and I found no authoritative figure. Do not
print one.

## 2. Moonscape Overlook — CLOSED

### Verbatim BLM directions

> "**From Hanksville to Factory Butte Road** — Drive west on highway 24 for **10 miles**, turn right
> onto **BLM Rd #0091 (also signed as 6650 east)** shortly after passing **mile marker 106**.
>
> **Head North on Factory Butte Road** — The road is **unpaved but generally well maintained**. In a
> half mile there will be **restrooms and an information kiosk**. Keep to the right at this junction
> and continue for **3 miles**.
>
> **Turn Right on BLM Rd #0913** — The turnoff will be signed as BLM road 0913. **A high clearance
> vehicle is recommended beyond this point.**
>
> **Turn Left on Skyline View Road (BLM Rd #0913 cont.)** — Continue north for **2 miles**, take a
> right at the junction and the moonscape overlook is **half a mile further at the end of the road**."

> "Perched atop the **Skyline Rim at the edge of Factory Bench**, this short trip offers beautiful views
> looking across the colorful and intricate features that make up the **Lower Blue Hills** area."

> "There are **no restrooms or facilities at the overlook**, please plan ahead and be prepared."

Source: <https://www.blm.gov/sites/default/files/docs/2026-04/Moonscape%20Overlook%202025.pdf>

### Answers to the questions asked

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| Distance from Hanksville | **10 mi paved on UT-24, then ~6 mi of dirt = ~16 mi one way.** Budget **35–45 min each way** driving. |
| Road surface | Two grades. **Segment A (BLM Rd 0091 / Factory Butte Rd, ~3.5 mi):** graded, "unpaved but generally well maintained", clay/gravel. **Segment B (BLM Rd 0913 / Skyline View Rd, ~2.5 mi):** narrower unmaintained clay-and-rock two-track. |
| Vehicle class genuinely required | **BLM's own words: "A high clearance vehicle is recommended beyond this point" — the point being the BLM Rd 0913 turnoff.** So: **any car reaches the kiosk; a high-clearance vehicle (NPS defines this as ≥8 in ground clearance — see §5) is the stated requirement for the last ~2.5 mi.** 4WD is **not** stated as required by BLM in dry conditions. A standard rental SUV/crossover, dry, driven slowly, is the right tool. A sedan should stop at the kiosk. |
| Turnaround / parking | **Yes — the overlook is at the dead end of the road** ("half a mile further at the end of the road"). It is a road-end promontory, not a pull-off. `GAP: BLM does not describe the size of the parking area or state a vehicle-turning limit.` Corroborating description: the overlook is a promontory "along Skyline Rim, looking out over a vast, barren landscape", reached by a side track off Factory Bench Road — <https://www.americansouthwest.net/utah/factory-butte/index.html> |
| Exposure risk at the rim | **Official and explicit.** BLM: "**Sandstone can be unstable, avoid playing around cliff edges.**" There is **no fence, no railing, no signage at the edge.** The photogenic feature is a narrow rock tongue jutting out over the drop. Capitol Reef Country describes "the narrow, iconic ridge that juts into the abyss" — <https://capitolreefcountry.com/moonscape-overlook/> |

### The child-safety call — state this plainly in the itinerary

**Moonscape Overlook is the single highest-consequence spot in the Utah leg for an 11-year-old.**
It is an **unfenced, undercut cliff rim on unstable sandstone**, at the **end of a 6-mile dirt road**,
with **no cell coverage** (BLM: "cell coverage is scarce in the region") and **no facilities**. BLM's
warning is not boilerplate — it names *unstable sandstone* and *cliff edges* specifically.

Practical rule to put in the plan: **hand-hold or a hard stop-line 3 m back from the rim; nobody walks
out onto the projecting fin; the adult with the camera is not the adult supervising the child.** The
view is fully delivered from well back — walking out on the fin buys a photograph, not a view.

Other BLM warnings on the same page, verbatim:

> "Many routes are not marked and require navigation skills. **GPS and maps are recommended as cell
> coverage is scarce in the region.**"
> "Due to high heat exposure this area is **best visited either in the Spring and Fall season, or early
> in the morning and late afternoon.**"

Mid-to-late September falls in BLM's own recommended season, and this is a **sunset** subject
(the rim faces out over the Lower Blue Hills to the west/north-west).

`GAP: mileage discrepancy on segment A.` BLM's PDF says 0.5 mi to the kiosk then **3 more miles** to
the BLM 0913 turnoff (3.5 mi total). Several third-party guides say **6.0 miles** north on 6650 E
before the 0913 turnoff. **Trust BLM but watch the odometer and the road signs — 0913 is signed.**

`GAP: no published GPS coordinate for the overlook from BLM or any government source.` Do not print
one. Navigate by the signed BLM road numbers (0091 → 0913 → Skyline View Rd), which BLM confirms are
posted, and by downloaded offline maps.

## 3. Bentonite Hills — CLOSED, and the prior research had the wrong hill

**This is the most important correction in this document.**

BLM states there are **two** places called the Bentonite Hills, verbatim:

> "This driving tour will take you through an otherworldly desert with a peak at the Mars Desert
> Research Station, **one of two places commonly referred to as the 'Bentonite Hills'**, and an
> exploration around an active paleontology dig."

> "**Getting There / From Hanksville** — The beginning of **Cow Dung road** is an **unmarked turnoff on
> your right shortly after passing mile marker 113**."

> "**Bentonite Hills** — While there is no singular spot designated as the bentonite hills, **many of
> the most colorful examples of this shale are located around 4 miles in.** Keep foot traffic to
> established paths please."

> "**Mars Desert Research Station** — MDRS is located **3.2 miles down Cow Dung road** and has a
> **designated viewing area to park at**, note that the station is **not open to the public**; please
> observe only from the viewing area. **Drone flights are not allowed at MDRS.**"

> "**Burpee Museum Dinosaur Quarry** — The trailhead is **7.3 miles down the road** with an information
> kiosk detailing some of the fossils discovered on site. This is an **active dig site** with ongoing
> surveys, **removal of fossil materials is not permitted**."

Source: <https://www.blm.gov/sites/default/files/docs/2026-04/Blue%20Valley_Burpee%20Quary.pdf>

### The answer to the question asked

**Do NOT route to the Bentonite Hills via Cathedral Valley Road / the Hartnet. Use the BLM Cow Dung
Road hills instead.**

- **Cow Dung Road version (the one to do):** turnoff on UT-24 **shortly after MP 113, ~3.4 mi west of
  Hanksville**, north side. Best colour is **~4 miles in**. **Zero river crossings. No ford. No NPS
  land. No fee. No permit.** Round trip from Hanksville: **~15 miles, ~1 hour of driving**, and you can
  bolt on the MDRS viewing area at 3.2 mi and the Burpee dinosaur quarry kiosk at 7.3 mi on the same
  road. **This fully answers the brief: the UT-24-side access does not require the Fremont River ford,
  because it is a different road on different land entirely.**
- **Cathedral Valley / Hartnet Road version (the NPS one):** this is the one the ford problem attaches
  to, and prior research was right that it is out. **Confirmed live as of 2026-09-05:** the NPS Capitol
  Reef road-conditions table currently lists **"River Ford — Impassable"** and **"Hartnet Road —
  Impassable"**, with Cathedral Valley itself "HC4WD to Temples, Impassable beyond."
  <https://www.nps.gov/care/planyourvisit/conditions.htm>

`GAP: BLM gives no vehicle class and no surface description for Cow Dung Road itself.` The PDF's
general warning ("Most roads in this area are clay-based and can become impassable quickly after rain
and snow") is the only official statement. Third-party consensus is that Cow Dung Rd is a graded,
occasionally rutted dirt road that a **passenger car handles slowly when dry**, and that a
**high-clearance vehicle is preferable when it has been freshly graded or recently rutted** —
see <https://www.jaredsdetours.com/bentonite-hills-utah/> and
<https://www.hanksvilleutah.gov/mars-on-earth>. **Treat as: dry = crossover fine; wet = do not.**
**Close this by phone — see §7.**

**Drone note:** BLM explicitly prohibits drone flights at MDRS. This is a separate, specific
prohibition from the NPS blanket ban already captured in `research-logistics.md` §10.

## 4. Factory Butte / Swing Arm City — CLOSED

### Road surface and access

- **Location:** "Factory Butte is located **12 miles west of Hanksville, Utah on State Route 24**."
  Managed by the Henry Mountains Field Station. **No fees.** "There is a **restroom and interpretive
  kiosks** at Factory Butte." <https://www.blm.gov/visit/factory-butte-recreation-area>
- **The access road has a name and a number, and it is the same road as the Moonscape approach for its
  first 3.5 miles: BLM Rd #0091, signed "6650 East", also called Factory Butte Road / Coal Mine Road /
  North Factory Butte Road.** BLM: "The road is **unpaved but generally well maintained**."
  <https://www.blm.gov/sites/default/files/docs/2026-04/Moonscape%20Overlook%202025.pdf>
  — **this closes the `GAP` in `research-trails.md` §4.3 about the access road name and surface.**
- **Factory Bench Road** (the road along the butte's east side, north of the highway) is described by
  americansouthwest.net as "**suitable for any vehicle (when dry) for at least ten miles**" before it
  roughens near Salt Wash, and "**well maintained by the BLM**" with information boards and primitive
  camping. <https://www.americansouthwest.net/utah/factory-butte/index.html>
- **2WD verdict:** BLM's own framing is "passenger car touring", and the graded 0091/Factory Bench
  roads bear that out **when dry**. **A 2WD car is fine to the kiosk and along the graded bench road.**

### BLM designation and current OHV status — current and confirmed

- **Designation: Factory Butte Special Recreation Management Area (SRMA), designated October 2008**,
  under the **Richfield Field Office Resource Management Plan**, BLM **Color Country District**.
- **Three OHV open areas totalling ~8,000 acres**, verbatim from the BLM brochure:
  - **Swing Arm City — 2,600 acres** (BLM press release: 2,602 ac). "popular, high adrenalin
    hill-climbs for both beginners and experienced riders and is **the most easily accessible open
    area** within Factory Butte SRMA."
  - **Factory Butte OHV Open Area — 5,300 acres.** "Access is from the **Factory Bench Road** on the
    eastern boundary of the open area."
  - **Caineville Cove — about 100 acres**, "open right behind the Motel", low-adrenalin youth riding.
- **Current status: OPEN.** The Factory Butte and Caineville Cove areas were **reopened 22 May 2019**
  when BLM rescinded a 2006 travel restriction, after **10 years of annual monitoring since 2009** with
  the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service to protect endangered cactus. **5,400 acres** were reopened.
  <https://www.blm.gov/press-release/blm-opens-5400-acres-ohv> — BLM's live Factory Butte visit page
  still carries this as its current status line, so **the 2019 opening stands as of this check
  (2026-09-05)**.
- **The rule that matters to a non-OHV visitor:** "**All travel outside the designated open areas is
  either limited to designated routes or closed to motorized use.**" ESA violation: **maximum fine
  $50,000 and up to a year in prison.** Stay on numbered roads; do not walk on the cactus flats.
- **Facilities:** "There is a **vault toilet facility for visitors on Factory Bench Road on the east
  side of Swing Arm City**", plus the restroom/kiosk 0.5 mi up BLM Rd 0091.
- **Cell service, verbatim:** "**Cellular phone service is available in several locations on Factory
  Bench Road and in Hanksville, Utah.**" This is a meaningful qualifier on the blanket "no coverage"
  assumption in `research-logistics.md` §7 — but do not rely on it.
- **Nearest emergency medical, verbatim:** "Ambulance and EMT services respond from Hanksville. The
  nearest emergency medical facility is located in **Bicknell, Utah at the Wayne County Community
  Health Center, 128 South 300 West, 435-425-3744**." Bicknell is ~60 mi west via UT-24.

Source for all brochure quotes:
<https://www.blm.gov/sites/default/files/documents/files/BLMUtahFinalFactoryButte_Brochure.pdf>

### Where the classic photograph is actually taken from

Three distinct shots, and they are not the same place:

1. **The postcard butte-with-fluted-badlands shot** — from **Coal Mine Road / BLM Rd 0091 / Factory
   Bench Road**, north off UT-24 about 11 miles west of Hanksville. "There's **ample parking just north
   of the highway in a very large open area and all along Coal Mine Road**", and the road "runs along
   the eastern side of the butte and curves around the northern end." Best light is "**early morning or
   just before sunset**" — "the low angle of the sun makes for some incredibly dramatic effects on the
   formation itself and the badlands surrounding it."
   <https://capitolreefcountry.com/attractions/factory-butte/> and
   <https://www.americansouthwest.net/utah/factory-butte/index.html>
2. **The wide badlands-panorama shot** — from **Moonscape Overlook / Skyline Rim** (§2), which looks
   out over the Lower Blue Hills rather than at the butte. Different subject, different drive.
3. **The delicate-formations shot** — Coal Mine Wash, north-west of the butte, "small, delicate
   formations including arches, narrow fins and tiny hoodoos", also a sunset subject.
   <https://www.americansouthwest.net/utah/factory-butte/index.html>

**Practical scheduling consequence:** #1 and #2 are both low-sun subjects and they are ~6 miles and
~30 minutes apart on the same road system. **You cannot shoot both at the same golden hour.** Pair
Factory Butte with sunrise (butte lit from the east) and Moonscape with sunset, or split them across
the two Hanksville days.

`GAP: BLM publishes no coordinates for a named Factory Butte viewpoint`, because there isn't one —
the "viewpoint" is the whole first few miles of Factory Bench Road. Approximate butte centre for
orientation only: **38.440, -110.917** (<https://www.americansouthwest.net/utah/factory-butte/index.html>).

## 5. THE WET-CLAY DECISION RULE — a checkable rule, not "avoid if wet"

### 5.1 The authoritative statements, ranked

**(a) BLM Utah, on how long — the "how long" answer the brief asked for:**

> "**Clay-based roads become impassable when wet. Weather conditions can render some roads impassable
> for days.**"

Source: BLM Utah, Skutumpah and Johnson Canyon Roads map/brochure —
<https://www.blm.gov/sites/default/files/documents/files/BLMUtahSkutumpahandJohnsonCanyonRoads.pdf>
(BLM Utah, GSENM. Different unit, same agency, same soil chemistry, and it is the only **official**
duration statement I could retrieve anywhere in BLM Utah's published material.)

**(b) BLM Henry Mountain Field Station, on these exact roads:**

> "**Most roads in this area are clay-based and can become impassable quickly after rain and snow,
> always check the weather forecast before departure.**"

Identical sentence appears in **both** the Moonscape and the Cow Dung Road PDFs, i.e. it is the field
station's standing statement for the whole Hanksville badlands road network.

**(c) NPS Capitol Reef, on severity (already in prior research, restated because it is the ceiling):**

> "Spring and summer rains and winter snows can leave the roads muddy, washed out, and **impassable to
> the best high-clearance four-wheel drive vehicle**." "**Help may not arrive for hours or even days.**"

<https://www.nps.gov/care/planyourvisit/cathedralvalley.htm>

**(d) NPS Capitol Reef, on what "high clearance" actually means — new, and useful for the rental
booking:** the park **defines high clearance as a minimum of 8 inches of ground clearance**, and notes
that outside agencies often require **9 inches or more**.
<https://www.nps.gov/care/planyourvisit/conditions.htm>
*Reference points: a Toyota RAV4 is ~8.4 in, a Subaru Outback ~8.7 in, a Chevrolet Equinox ~7.6 in, a
mid-size sedan ~5.5 in. Book the class deliberately.*

`GAP: no source, official or otherwise, states a specific drying time for the Hanksville / Factory
Butte roads.` The best available official duration is BLM Utah's "**impassable for days**". Widely
repeated but **unofficial** community figures are **24–48 hours of sun and wind** to dry, with reports
of a party waiting 36 hours to drive out and a couple stuck two days near Factory Butte
(<https://community.goodsam.com/discussions/campgrounds/southern-utah-boondocking-how-long-do-roads-take-to-dry/3346740>,
<https://backcountrypost.com/threads/driving-on-wet-clay.7693/>). **Use 48 hours as the planning
number and treat it as a floor, not a guarantee.**

### 5.2 The checkable rule — put this verbatim in the itinerary

> **HANKSVILLE DIRT-ROAD GO / NO-GO — run this the night before AND at breakfast.**
>
> **Step 1 — Observed rain, last 72 h.** Query the Goblin Valley State Park COOP gauge (station
> `USC00423254`, 14 mi north of Hanksville, the nearest gauge that is actually reporting):
> ```
> curl -s -X POST https://data.rcc-acis.org/StnData -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
>   -d '{"sid":"USC00423254","sdate":"YYYY-MM-DD","edate":"YYYY-MM-DD","elems":"pcpn"}'
> ```
> **Any non-zero daily total in the previous 48 h → NO-GO on BLM Rd 0913 / Skyline View Rd / Cow Dung
> Rd / BLM Rd 1574. Any non-zero total in the previous 24 h → NO-GO on dirt of any kind, including the
> graded BLM Rd 0091.**
>
> **Step 2 — Forecast, today and tonight.** NWS Salt Lake City, forecast zone **UTZ130 "Western
> Canyonlands"**, grid **SLC/128,63**:
> <https://forecast.weather.gov/MapClick.php?lat=38.3725&lon=-110.7151> ·
> <https://api.weather.gov/gridpoints/SLC/128,63/forecast>
> **Probability of precipitation ≥ 20% at any point in the day → NO-GO.** You do not want to be 6 miles
> up a clay road when a cell arrives; BLM says these roads go "impassable **quickly**".
>
> **Step 3 — Current conditions at the trailhead town.** Hanksville Airport ASOS **KHVE**:
> <https://api.weather.gov/stations/KHVE/observations/latest>
> Use for sky/wind/temperature only. **Caveat: KHVE does not report precipitation** — its
> `precipitationLastHour/3Hours/6Hours` fields return null, and its COOP precipitation record ends
> 2025-08-31. **Do not use KHVE to decide whether it rained.** That is what Step 1 is for.
>
> **Step 4 — Human confirmation, if any doubt survives steps 1–3.** Call **BLM Henry Mountains Field
> Station, (435) 542-3461** or **(435) 701-2360**, open **08:00–16:30**. This is the office that
> publishes the two PDFs above and it is *in Hanksville*, 380 South 100 West.
> **Backstop, available 24/7 as an automated line:** **Capitol Reef NP road conditions,
> (435) 425-3791, press 4.** It reports the Hartnet / Cathedral / River Ford status — the same
> bentonite, 20 miles west. **If NPS says Hartnet is impassable, assume the BLM clay roads are too.**
>
> **There is no "drive carefully" version of this decision.** BLM and NPS both state that wet bentonite
> defeats the best 4WD. Wet = the Hanksville days become the Capitol Reef Scenic Drive (paved) and
> Goblin Valley (paved to the visitor centre), and you lose nothing but the photographs.

## 6. Fuel and last services before the dirt — CONFIRMED

### What Hanksville actually has

Per the town's own site (<https://www.hanksvilleutah.gov/fuel>), **two public fuel stations**:

- **Hollow Mountain** — the station built into the rock face; fuel, gift shop, snacks, souvenirs.
- **Stan's Fuel & Foodmart** — on Highway 95; fuel, food, drinks, snacks, supplies.
- (A third, the **UDOT fleet station at the state road shed**, is **24/7 but fleet-card only** — not
  available to travellers. Do not count it.)

The town site also lists categories for **Food, Lodging and Adventure/Recreation**
(<https://www.hanksvilleutah.gov/>), i.e. Hanksville has restaurants and motels but is a very small
town. **Town Office: 435.542.3451, clerk@hanksvilleutah.gov, Tue–Thu 10:00–14:00.**

`GAP: neither the town site nor any official source publishes station opening hours.` The town page
references "24-hour pumping" without saying which station offers it. **Assume card-at-pump only after
dark and do not rely on the shop being open.** `GAP: no grocery store, mechanic, towing service, ATM
or bank is listed on any official page.` Nearest emergency medical is **Bicknell, ~60 mi west**
(Wayne County Community Health Center, 435-425-3744, per the BLM Factory Butte brochure).

### Hite — confirmed closed, in NPS's own words

> "**All services at Hite are closed until further notice.**"

The **Hite Ranger Station is closed** and the Cataract Canyon boat ramp at North Wash is inoperable.
Backcountry permits for the Orange Cliffs moved to Hans Flat Ranger Station (435-719-2218). NPS names
**Blanding, 70 miles away**, as the nearest retail/motel/medical.
Source: <https://www.nps.gov/glca/planyourvisit/hite.htm>

**This confirms `research-logistics.md` §8.5(1) exactly: UT-95 Hanksville → Blanding has no fuel, and
Hite is not a fallback.**

### The fuel rule for days 8–9, restated with the dirt added

The Hanksville dirt loops add **~30–40 miles of low-gear, low-mpg driving** on top of whatever the
highway legs cost. Neither Factory Butte, Moonscape, the Bentonite Hills nor Blue Valley Spire has
fuel, water, or a phone.

> **Fill the tank in Hanksville before every dirt excursion, not just before UT-95.** Leave town with
> a full tank, more water than you think, and a downloaded offline map. BLM: "GPS and maps are
> recommended as cell coverage is scarce in the region."

## 8. Net verdict table — replaces `research-trails.md` §4.6

| Destination | Drive from Hanksville | Dirt | Vehicle, DRY | Walk | Exposure | Wet | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Blue Valley Spire** | ~7 mi W on UT-24 to MP 109.35 | **1.2 mi**, BLM Rd 1574 | Crossover/SUV comfortably; low sedan marginal | **1.6–2.3 mi RT, 173 ft** | **None** — flat valley floor | **NO** | **High** (BLM PDF + RTR with GPS track) |
| **Bentonite Hills (Cow Dung Rd)** | ~3.4 mi W to MP 113 | **~4 mi** each way | Car OK slowly; crossover better | Roadside; stay on established paths | None | **NO** | **High** (BLM PDF) — vehicle class is the only gap |
| **Factory Butte viewpoints** | ~10–12 mi W, BLM Rd 0091 / Factory Bench Rd | 0.5–10 mi, graded | **2WD passenger car OK** | None required | None | **NO** | **High** (BLM) |
| **Moonscape Overlook** | ~10 mi W then ~6 mi dirt (~16 mi) | **~6 mi**; last ~2.5 mi rough | **High clearance (≥8 in) recommended by BLM**; 4WD not stated as required | ~50 m from car | **HIGH — unfenced unstable-sandstone cliff rim** | **NO** | **High** (BLM PDF) |
| **Cathedral Valley full loop / Fremont River ford** | — | — | — | — | — | **OUT** — NPS currently lists River Ford and Hartnet Road as **Impassable** (checked 2026-09-05) | **High** (NPS live) |

**One-line planning answer:** all four Hanksville stops are now sourced to BLM's own field station,
all four are short walks off graded-to-rough clay roads, the Bentonite Hills question dissolves once
you use the BLM Cow Dung Road hills instead of the NPS Hartnet ones, **the only two real risks left
are wet clay (§5.2 gives you a numeric go/no-go) and the unfenced rim at Moonscape (§2).**
